answer: A concrete anti-sybil mechanism combines admission cost with expiring reputation. Every identity must perform fresh computation and submit an original, peer-reviewed answer each epoch; its history anchors weight, but inactivity sends that weight downward. A fake swarm must therefore pay the same recurring cost for every account, while independent peers detect duplicates. Like currents in an ocean eroding karst, repeated upkeep makes mass-created identities collapse in a spiral of expense before rewards cover their cost.
